operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: 'City','Country','IATA','ICAO','Type','Principal_activities','Incorporated_in','Group_Equity_Shareholding','Vehicle_Flight_number','Date','Pilot','Velocity','Altitude' — must be double-quoted verbatim; column lookup case-insensitive.
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent table in FK: references `airport`("id") — sqlite_master DDL replay must keep backticks; sqlparse/identifier handling must not choke.
All columns notnull=0 (no NOT NULL constraints) and no CHECK/UNIQUE — so step-1 insert failures are rare; PKs are the only real constraint.
Tiny tables: airport=9, operate_company=14, flight=13 rows; choose_table_sizes (30..2500) will massively over-generate vs original — expected.
Declared type 'INT' (not 'INTEGER') dispatches to Number via 'int' substring; 'REAL' -> Number; 'TEXT' -> String. No crash-fallback columns here.
flight.Date is TEXT storing 'March 1, 1963' style — declared type dispatches to String fuzzer, NOT Date fuzzer; text-stored dates will be fuzzed as random strings.
flight.Vehicle_Flight_number stores 'M2-F1 #0' — '#' and space in values; String fuzzer charset a-zA-Z 0-9() will not reproduce '#'.
FKs: flight.airport_id -> airport.id, flight.company_id -> operate_company.id; both parents exist and are unique PKs; no self-refs, no composite keys, no dangling FKs.
airport_id distinct=8 < 9 airports, company_id distinct=10 < 14 companies — original already has unused parents; FK fill with replacement is fine.
Group_Equity_Shareholding REAL values 18.77..100.0; Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) -> default scale, will produce wide floats.
Pilot has only 2 distinct values (Thompson, Peterson); Velocity/Altitude only 2 distinct each — heavy ties in original.
No views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs; DDL replay is just 3 CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: airport/operate_company/flight id columns: Number fuzzer, int perturbation (+-1,+-2) around sampled originals — PKs stay near 1..14, duplicates dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
flight.Date: String fuzzer (declared TEXT) — random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() plus contamination, NOT date-shaped; any gold query filtering on date format will get implausible values (FN risk).
flight.Vehicle_Flight_number: String fuzzer — loses 'M2-F1 #N' pattern; gold queries matching '#' or prefix will miss (FN).
City/Country/IATA/ICAO/name/Type/Principal_activities/Incorporated_in: String fuzzer with 5 sampled originals + literal pool; contamination adds junk suffixes (FN on equality/join).
Pilot: only 2 originals -> String sampler mostly reuses 'Thompson'/'Peterson' with contamination; ties abundant (FP risk on DISTINCT/COUNT).
Velocity/Altitude: Number fuzzer, 2 originals -> list range [min, 10^scale] quirk gives huge upper bound; values far from 0/3650 (FN on range predicates).
Group_Equity_Shareholding: Number fuzzer, 7 originals, real scale — plausible-ish but perturbed +-0.01/0.02.
FK columns airport_id/company_id: drawn from parent's FINAL filtered id list with replacement -> referential integrity holds, but many-to-one ties (FP on COUNT DISTINCT).
Table sizes 30..2500 vs original 9/14/13 -> cardinality-based gold (COUNT) will differ wildly; TS relies on result_eq not on matching original counts.
No NOT NULL/CHECK -> almost no insert failures; rows_ok ~= requested size.
Date-as-string means gold queries using strftime/date() on flight.Date will error or return NULL on fuzzed values (sql_b error -> False in execute_and_compare).
Literal pool from train SQL will inject real City/Country/IATA strings, partially rescuing String columns; Date column gets no date literals unless train SQL has them.
